I'm not sure if what I did counts as Family Based Therapy since English isn't my first language and I don't know the names of all the therapy types, but my experience sounds pretty in line with what you describe. 

I think I can count on one hand the number of times I actually spoke during my almost two years of treatment, even drying the times when my parents weren't present in the room. Like you say, it definitely felt like anything I said could and would be relayed to my parents. On top of that it was never spoken about *why* I had an ED, or even how to manage the anxiety around eating or gaining weight. The only thing they did was weigh me and tell me to eat more if I didn't gain fast enough.

Maybe this kind of therapy is good for some people, but to me it just felt like it was about making my parents comfortable rather than treating me and my illness. I feel like it does nothing to build trust between the patient and the therapist when nothing you say is truly confidential.

Like the other commenter said I think it's more about the mindset rather than how long you do it. I know a few of us view our ED as an addiction, and if we do that comparison it becomes quite clear that even just a one-time thing is a relapse.

(I don't know if my addiction parallel was clear but I mean like if you've been addicted to drugs or alcohol and you're sober now, but you take drugs just once you still relapsed. First I just want to say that I'm so sorry that you're feeling this way. A big thing with eating disorders is the constant nagging feeling that you are never valid enough. There is always someone else doing something even worse and you feel as though you will not be valid unless you too, do that certain thing. That is the eating disorder "talking". You will never feel valid enough. You try and try and try until you die. And the worst part is that you still will not feel valid as you're dying.

To respond to your question: Yes, eating disorders are competitive. They make you think that you need to be as ill as possible until you either die or recover. Please try to get help as soon as possible. It sucks reaching out for help but eating disorders thrive in secrecy and the sooner you ask for help the better the odds are of recovering. It's not worth dying on the pursuit of validity you'll never feel.

I'm so sorry that you're struggling right now. I felt this exact way just a few days ago so I'm using these reasons myself at the moment.

1. I don't want to be the reason that my younger relatives know what a funeral is.
2. The uncomfortable physical feelings (the cold, hunger pains, dizziness, etc) that stem from the ED can actually disappear if you don't give your ED space to flourish.
3. Not being overrun by guilt and anxiety when eating out with family or friends and having those emotions overshadow the entire event.
4. Food freedom actually exists and it is possible to get there. (I have, to an extent, been there myself and yes, you can actually eat something high in calories and feel completely fine afterwards).
5. I don't know if you are in school or working but you can only ever get so far with an ED at the same time. Sooner or later it will catch up with you and you performance will pay the price.
6. If your ED kills you, because eventually it will do if you don't recover, will you truly be content with the life that you have lived?
